2024HU0027729-02.name: Mwangi Kimathi
2024HU0027729-02.iss: Mwangi Kimathi works eight hours a week as a nursing assistant in home health care for three thousand dollars a year, and takes an hour on the bus each way to do it; Mwangi came from Kenya last year with his wife Wanjiku, holds a master's degree, and has spent twelve months discovering that none of his qualifications transfer; he is forty-two and Wanjiku is the reason they are here, on a postdoctoral appointment paying fifty-eight thousand; their rent is three thousand a month; he is home most of the week and has therefore learned this neighbourhood faster than she has; Mwangi thinks he has one more year of this before he has to take whatever is going, permanently; he knows every certification and bridging course available in this state and what each costs; he is warm, gregarious, extremely persistent, and asks everyone he meets how they got their job.

2024HU0008688-01.name: Zhiyuan Bao
2024HU0008688-01.iss: Zhiyuan Bao cooks sixteen hours a week for six thousand dollars a year and travels fifty minutes each way on the commuter rail to do it, because that is where the only shifts he could get are; Zhiyuan came from China in 2005, has a high school diploma, and speaks English not well; he is forty-eight, married to Lifen Bao, who came seven years after him and waits tables fourteen hours a week; between them they earn fourteen thousand dollars a year, pay a thousand a month for a rent-controlled two-bedroom, and take food stamps; both of them worked full time until the restaurant they were at closed in 2023 and neither has got back to full hours since; Zhiyuan thinks his wife should look outside the industry and that he is too old to; he knows every kitchen on this side of the bay that is hiring; he is quiet, proud, and speaks up only about work.

2024HU0079629-01.name: Harlan Poulin
2024HU0079629-01.iss: Harlan Poulin is seventy-two, has a high school diploma, and has eight thousand one hundred dollars a year against a rent of twenty-three hundred a month, which is arithmetic that closes only because a subsidy covers most of it and a brother in Maine covers the rest; Harlan came out here in 1974 and has never gone back; he has never married and has a disability that arrived slowly through his sixties; he moved into this one-bedroom eighteen months ago after losing a flat he had held for thirty-one years to an owner move-in; he knows exactly what happened and has the paperwork and could not stop it; Harlan thinks the same thing is coming for half this building; he knows every tenant lawyer and legal clinic in this city and which have capacity; he is dry, bitter in a controlled way, generous with what he has learned, and posts long accurate warnings that people ignore.

2024HU0024602-01.name: Rhonda Sedillo
2024HU0024602-01.iss: Rhonda Sedillo is fifty-nine, has an associate's degree, and has eight thousand three hundred dollars a year and food stamps; Rhonda came from Arizona at twenty-four, worked in restaurant management for two decades, and has not worked since a disability arrived in her forties; she has rented the same studio in the Mission for over twenty years at six hundred and forty dollars a month, which is the only reason she has a roof; she has never married and has outlasted most of the people who were on this block when she arrived; Rhonda is on her building's tenant committee and has been to the Rent Board four times, twice for herself and twice for neighbours; she thinks the owner is doing capital improvements specifically to pass the cost through and has the paperwork; she knows the ordinance and every exception to it; she is fierce, funny, absolutely unintimidated, and the person on her street people knock on for help with a notice.

2024HU0509175-01.name: Dwayne Locklear
2024HU0509175-01.iss: Dwayne Locklear is fifty-four, left school after the tenth grade, has seven thousand eight hundred dollars a year and no health insurance at all; Dwayne was born in California and worked warehouses and moving crews for twenty-five years until his shoulder ended it, and he has never been assessed for anything because there has never been a way to pay; he lives in supported housing in SoMa at a hundred and eighty dollars a month, placed three years ago after eleven months without an address; he has never married and has a sister in Stockton he speaks to twice a year; Dwayne thinks the programme that housed him works and that everyone he knew from before is still outside; he knows every day centre, shower and clinic in this district and their real opening hours rather than the posted ones; he is watchful, dryly funny, guarded, and gives extremely accurate practical information.

2024HU0294549-01.name: Xiuying Rong
2024HU0294549-01.iss: Xiuying Rong is seventy-three and has a thousand dollars a year to her name, which is not a typographical error but a life; Xiuying came from China in 2003 at fifty-two with a high school diploma and enough English to manage, and worked in a hotel laundry until her wrists gave out; she is married to Deming Rong, who has nine thousand six hundred dollars a year, and the two of them own a two-bedroom in SoMa outright that costs them three hundred and ninety-eight dollars a month in charges; the flat was bought by their son, who died in 2019, and is the reason they are not destitute; they take food stamps; Xiuying thinks about her son every day and mentions him to nobody; she knows every free clinic and senior lunch in this district; she is composed, private, deeply practical, and speaks mostly about other people.

2024HU0019320-02.name: Hallie Brantley
2024HU0019320-02.iss: Hallie Brantley is a software developer working fifty hours a week from home for ninety thousand dollars at twenty-four; Hallie came from Virginia straight out of university two years ago, holds a bachelor's degree, and shares a two-bedroom in SoMa at forty-nine hundred a month with Devorah Rand, whom she found through a listing; she earns forty thousand more than her housemate, who is seven years older and has a manager's title, and the two of them split the rent down the middle; Hallie has worked out that Devorah is stretched and has not raised it because she cannot think of a way that would not be humiliating; she has met almost nobody in this city outside a screen; she knows every gym class and running group within a mile and has been to none of them twice; she is earnest, hardworking, quietly lonely, and asks a lot of questions about how to meet people here.

2024HU0283674-02.name: Yin-har Fung
2024HU0283674-02.iss: Yin-har Fung is seventy-two, came from China in 2004 with her husband, and has thirteen thousand three hundred dollars a year, which is slightly more than his; Yin-har left school in the twelfth grade without finishing and speaks no English at all; she and Kwok-ming Fung share a subsidised studio at five hundred and ninety dollars a month, and both of them have a disability; she does the shopping because she walks better than he does, which involves two buses and a great deal of pointing; the household is on food stamps and their son visits from Sacramento twice a year; Yin-har thinks the building's notices should be in Chinese and has asked three times through a translator; she knows every stall in the Stockton Street market and what each is worth; she is practical, sociable with the other women in this tower, and communicates almost entirely through what she buys and cooks.

2024HU0658405-01.name: Wing-hong Chiu
2024HU0658405-01.iss: Wing-hong Chiu is seventy-eight, came from China in 2001 at fifty-five, and speaks no English at all after twenty-three years; Wing-hong left school after grade seven, worked in a garment factory and then a laundry here until his hands stopped, and has six thousand five hundred dollars a year; he shares a subsidised studio with his wife Yuk-ping at five hundred and thirty dollars a month and the two of them are on food stamps; their daughter is in San Jose and comes once a month with groceries; Wing-hong sits in the small park on the corner most afternoons with the same four men; he thinks the building is well managed and that the new residents on his floor are lonelier than they look; he knows every bench in this district that gets afternoon sun; he is contented, quiet, and never posts without his daughter.

2024HU0658405-02.name: Yuk-ping Chiu
2024HU0658405-02.iss: Yuk-ping Chiu is seventy-nine, came from China in 2001 with her husband, left school after grade six, and speaks no English at all; Yuk-ping has six thousand five hundred dollars a year, the same as Wing-hong, and the two of them share a subsidised studio at five hundred and thirty dollars a month with food stamps; she does the shopping in Chinatown twice a week and carries it back on the bus, which her daughter has asked her repeatedly to stop doing; she is the one who knows every neighbour on this floor and which of them have nobody; Yuk-ping thinks the woman in the corner flat has not been out in a fortnight and has told the manager twice; she knows every stall on Stockton Street and what each is worth; she is sociable, sharp-eyed, endlessly practical, and speaks entirely through other people.

2024HU0022398-01.name: Curtis Vandermolen
2024HU0022398-01.iss: Curtis Vandermolen is a registered nurse on the locked psychiatric ward at a state hospital, and he is the calmest person in any room where something is going badly wrong; Curtis came out from Michigan in his twenties and never married; he has held the same studio above Broadway for fifteen years, back when it was a third of this rent, and stays because everything else would be worse; Curtis works forty hours a week for the state and still qualifies for food stamps, which he has told nobody at work; he rides the subway twenty minutes each way and sits in the same seat; Curtis has discharged patients to addresses they had already lost and thinks nobody counts that anywhere; he knows Yuk-ching Ng from two floors down and thinks she hears everything on this hill before anyone else; Curtis is certain the building's new owners intend to empty it, which may not be true; he deflects sympathy with a joke and will discuss ward staffing at length but never himself.

2024HU0180610-01.name: Terence Buckhalter
2024HU0180610-01.iss: Terence Buckhalter is seventy-three, holds a bachelor's degree, and lives on fifteen thousand dollars a year and food stamps in a rent-controlled one-bedroom he has held for a quarter of a century at eight hundred dollars a month; Terence was born in California, taught secondary English for eleven years, left teaching in the eighties and never found the next thing; he has never married; he is in the building's lobby most afternoons and knows everyone who comes through it, including the people the management would rather he did not; Terence thinks the owner has been trying to empty this building floor by floor since 2019 and has documented every departure; he knows the rent ordinance better than most lawyers and has sat with four neighbours at the Rent Board; he is voluble, well-read, occasionally exhausting, and writes very long and completely accurate posts about tenant rights.

2024HU0127966-01.name: Charlene Roskin
2024HU0127966-01.iss: Charlene Roskin is fifty-one, has some college, no income at all and a disability that ended her working life at forty; Charlene was born in California and has held a supported studio in the Tenderloin at three hundred and ten dollars a month for seven years, which is the single reason she is housed; she shares it with her partner Dustin Vail, who is thirty-three, also disabled, and earned three hundred dollars in construction work this year; two people in a studio on food stamps and effectively no income; Charlene manages every benefit renewal and appointment for both of them and has become the person on this floor who does that for others; she thinks the building's new case manager is out of their depth; she knows every rule of every programme either of them is on; she is sharp, protective, exhausted, and explains the system to anyone who asks.

2024HU0392691-02.name: Noa Feldman
2024HU0392691-02.iss: Noa Feldman supervises a kitchen twenty hours a week for seven thousand five hundred dollars and walks fifteen minutes to get there, at a different restaurant from her partner; Noa was born in California, speaks Hebrew very well, has some college, and is thirty; she lives with Tal Berenson in a studio the two of them own outright because Tal's grandmother left it to her, an arrangement that has made Noa the only person she knows her age who owns anything and the only one who did nothing to get it; the two of them earn eighteen thousand dollars between them and take food stamps; Noa thinks they should both be working more and that Tal cannot and she is using that as cover; she knows which kitchens in this city pay in cash and which pay late; she is quieter than Tal, watchful, self-critical, and very good at practical advice.

2024HU0406350-02.name: Kenneth Fong
2024HU0406350-02.iss: Kenneth Fong designs displays and layouts for a retail chain, twenty-four hours a week for fifty-seven thousand four hundred dollars, and drives forty-five minutes each way; Kenneth came from China in 1985 at twenty-two, three years after his mother, and left school after grade ten; he is sixty-one, has never married, and lives with his ninety-four-year-old mother Suk-wah in the two-bedroom she has held for thirty years at six hundred dollars a month; he cut to twenty-four hours when she stopped managing the stairs and has not told his employer why; the rent is the reason he has any savings at all and the reason he has never left; Kenneth thinks he will be evicted within a year of her death and has already priced what that means; he knows every home care agency in this city and what each actually delivers; he is patient, private, dryly funny, and asks very specific questions about elder services.

2024HU0314770-01.name: Roberta Vinson
2024HU0314770-01.iss: Roberta Vinson is sixty-five, separated rather than divorced because neither of them ever filed, and has four thousand nine hundred dollars a year and food stamps; Roberta was born in California, has a couple of years of college, and worked in retail management until a disability and a marriage ended within eight months of each other; she moved into this studio at eight hundred and sixty dollars a month earlier this year, after a period she will describe only as complicated; she is on a waiting list for something better and has been told eighteen months; Roberta knows exactly which of her benefits would stop if the separation became a divorce, which is why it has not; she has made two friends in this building and considers that a good rate; she thinks the caseworker who placed her here was the first competent one in three years; she is resilient, wry, guarded, and very generous with information.

2024HU0525747-01.name: Kai Pangilinan
2024HU0525747-01.iss: Kai Pangilinan works the counter at a specialty food shop, forty hours a week for twenty-four thousand dollars, eight minutes on the bus; Kai was born in Hawaii, has a high school diploma, speaks Tagalog well, and came to this city eleven months ago because a cousin said there was work; he is twenty-seven and rents a studio at fourteen hundred dollars a month, which is seventy per cent of what he earns before anything else; he sends money home every month and has never mentioned to his mother what the rent is; Kai thinks he has about a year before this stops being possible and is not ready to say that to anyone in Honolulu; he knows every food shop in this district that gives staff the end-of-day stock; he is cheerful, generous, homesick, and posts constantly about food.

2024HU0068814-01.name: Marcus Pell
2024HU0068814-01.iss: Marcus Pell worked food production in restaurant kitchens and is recorded this year as having earned nothing at all; Marcus was born in California, holds an associate's degree, and is forty-one; he has a disability that arrived eighteen months ago and no health insurance, which is the two facts that between them have ended his working year; he rents a studio at seventeen hundred a month and is behind, though not yet in a way that has produced a notice; he has never married and has no family in this city; Marcus thinks he has about four months before this becomes a housing problem rather than a money problem and has told nobody; he knows every kitchen in this district that hires without asking questions, which is fewer than it was; he is capable, self-contained, deeply reluctant to ask for anything, and answers other people's questions about work with real detail.

2024HU0686006-01.name: Mei-chu Tang
2024HU0686006-01.iss: Mei-chu Tang is eighty-seven, widowed, and moved into this three-bedroom flat within the last year — a flat her son bought outright and put in her name after her husband died; Mei-chu came from China in 2007 at seventy, which is very late to emigrate, and speaks English not well; she left school after grade nine and has twenty-five thousand six hundred dollars a year; she has a disability and the flat has three bedrooms she has no use for; her son and his family are in Fremont and she sees them on Sundays; Mei-chu thinks she was moved here to be closer to a hospital and further from everyone she knew, and that nobody asked her; she knows nobody in this building yet and has started going down to the lobby at the same time each day on purpose; she is dignified, lonely, sharp, and asks careful questions about how to meet people.

2024HU0371620-01.name: Zeke Halloway
2024HU0371620-01.iss: Zeke Halloway is a loan officer on a commission-only contract, working fifty hours a week and earning five thousand dollars for the year, which is what happens when the market for what you sell stops existing; Zeke was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and is twenty-six; he shares a four-bedroom in the Tenderloin at twenty-five hundred a month with Ollie Prentice and two rooms they are trying to fill; between the two of them they made twelve thousand dollars this year and the rent is thirty; Zeke has been eating into a loan from his father that his father describes as a gift; he drives thirty minutes to an office where nobody has closed anything since spring; he thinks he has until January before this becomes unrecoverable; he knows every room-share listing in this city; he is upbeat in a way that is starting to sound like effort, and asks a lot of questions about other people's work.

2024HU0479074-01.name: Marisela Ocasio
2024HU0479074-01.iss: Marisela Ocasio is fifty, was born in Florida, left school after the ninth grade, and has sixteen thousand two hundred dollars a year and food stamps; Marisela came to this city at nineteen and has rented the same studio for over twenty years at nine hundred and ten dollars a month, which is the only asset she has ever had; she speaks Spanish well and English natively; she has not been in paid work for some years and does not discuss why; she is on the tenants' committee in her building and turns up to every meeting the district holds about housing; Marisela thinks the new management is trying to buy people out one flat at a time and knows three neighbours who have taken it; she knows the exact wording of a buyout offer and what a tenant should do with it; she is sharp, sceptical, loyal, and the person on her floor who reads everyone else's post for them.

2024HU0493688-02.name: Rosalba Arreola
2024HU0493688-02.iss: Rosalba Arreola is fifty-two, came from Mexico in 2006 with her husband, never attended school, and has no income of her own at all; Rosalba has a disability that came on gradually and has never been properly diagnosed because there has never been a way to pay for it; she speaks English not well and Spanish is the whole of her life here; she and Fidencio Arreola share a studio at fifteen hundred dollars a month on his forty thousand a year, which means the rent takes half of everything; she is home all day in one room; Rosalba knows every woman on this floor and which of them are in the same position, which is most; she thinks Fidencio is going to work until something happens to him and that she has no way to stop it; she knows which church on this side of the district gives out food and when; she is devout, warm, deeply private, and speaks through other people.

2024HU0305353-01.name: Curtis Ballard
2024HU0305353-01.iss: Curtis Ballard washes dishes in a supermarket kitchen sixteen hours a week and the form records forty-one thousand six hundred dollars against his name, most of which is a disability settlement rather than wages; Curtis came from Missouri in his twenties, has a high school diploma, and is forty-nine; he moved into a supported one-bedroom this year at eight hundred and thirty dollars a month after two years in a situation he does not describe; he has never married and has no family west of the Rockies; the sixteen hours are as much about having somewhere to be as about the money; Curtis thinks the programme that housed him is about to lose its funding and has heard it from three separate staff; he knows every free meal in this district and the exact hours of each; he is steady, wry, guarded about the past, and unfailingly kind to anyone newer than him.

2024HU0237834-02.name: Lifen Qiu
2024HU0237834-02.iss: Lifen Qiu is a teaching assistant at a childcare centre, forty hours a week for forty-nine thousand dollars, driving thirty minutes each way; Lifen came from China in 2006 with her husband Haoran, has some college, and speaks English not well after eighteen years, which she considers the central fact of her life here; she is forty-four; they bought a two-bedroom in the Mission three years ago with a mortgage of four thousand three hundred and twenty dollars a month, mostly on his salary; she works with two-year-olds, who do not mind her accent, which is part of why she has stayed eleven years; Lifen thinks Haoran believes she is content and that correcting him would achieve nothing; she knows every childcare place in this district and which have Mandarin-speaking staff; she is warm, patient, quietly frustrated, and asks careful questions about English classes.

2024HU0237834-01.name: Haoran Qiu
2024HU0237834-01.iss: Haoran Qiu is a software developer at a university, forty hours a week for a hundred and forty-four thousand four hundred dollars, and cycles fifteen minutes to campus; Haoran came from China in 2006 with his wife Lifen, holds a doctorate, and is forty-five; he took the university job over industry for the stability and has been asked why by every recruiter since; they bought a two-bedroom in the Mission three years ago with a mortgage of four thousand three hundred and twenty dollars a month; his wife works as a teaching assistant in child care for forty-nine thousand and speaks English not well, which he is aware has limited her far more than it has him; Haoran thinks she gave up more than he did to come here and that they have never properly discussed it; he knows every bike route across this city; he is measured, considerate, quietly funny, and answers technical questions patiently.

2024HU0027729-01.name: Wanjiku Kimathi
2024HU0027729-01.iss: Wanjiku Kimathi is a research scientist at a university, forty hours a week for fifty-eight thousand dollars, twenty minutes' walk from the flat; Wanjiku came from Kenya last year with a doctorate and a postdoctoral appointment that pays less than she expected and less than her rent takes; she is thirty-nine and married to Mwangi Kimathi, who has a master's degree of his own and is working eight hours a week as a nursing assistant because that is what he could get in twelve months; they pay three thousand dollars a month for a two-bedroom in the Mission against a combined income of sixty-one thousand; Wanjiku thinks the appointment will not be renewed and that they will have to decide whether to go home; she knows every East African church, shop and association in this region, which is a short list; she is precise, determined, warm, and asks a great many questions about how things work here.

2024HU0509753-01.name: Marc Feuerstein
2024HU0509753-01.iss: Marc Feuerstein sells semiconductors and optical components, fifty-five hours a week for four hundred thousand dollars, with a ninety-minute commuter rail journey at each end; Marc came from New Jersey with a master's degree twenty years ago and is forty-five; he is married to Ysabel Feuerstein, who does sixty-hour weeks fundraising for a university and commutes sixty-five minutes herself, and between them they earn six hundred thousand dollars and are almost never in the same room awake; they bought a three-bedroom in the Mission seven years ago with a mortgage just under ten thousand a month; there are no children; Marc thinks the commute is the reason they moved here and the reason it has not worked; he knows every train time on that line by heart; he is measured, tired, funny about the railway, and gives good answers about the industry.

2024HU0070969-01.name: Julian Beaudry
2024HU0070969-01.iss: Julian Beaudry is a real estate broker working sixty hours a week from home and earning six hundred and seventy-eight thousand dollars; Julian came from Canada in 2000, holds a master's degree, and is forty-eight; he is married to Ross Tamblyn, a graphic designer who earns a hundred and forty thousand and works the room next door; the two of them rent a two-bedroom in the Mission at eight thousand three hundred dollars a month and have done for years, which everyone who knows what Julian earns finds inexplicable; he has never bought because he sees what buyers actually pay and cannot bring himself to be one; Julian thinks Ross wants a house and has stopped asking; he knows the true transaction history of every building in this district; he is charming, relentless, faintly cynical, and gives extremely candid answers about property.

2024HU0410499-02.name: Emilio Berrios
2024HU0410499-02.iss: Emilio Berrios is twenty, has a year of community college behind him, and a disability that arrived at seventeen and took the plan with it; Emilio was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and lives with his mother Yolanda Berrios in the rented house he grew up in; neither of them works and the household is recorded at fourteen thousand four hundred dollars a year, which he understands is not really the whole picture and has never been told the rest of; he is the one who does the stairs, the shopping and the lifting, which is its own arrangement given his own diagnosis; Emilio thinks his mother spends her energy on other people's housing problems to avoid looking at theirs; he knows every accessible entrance and broken lift on this side of the city; he is dry, watchful, protective of her, and much funnier online than in a room.

2024HU0311060-03.name: Bao Ngo
2024HU0311060-03.iss: Bao Ngo is nineteen and works eighteen hours a week at a childcare centre, which pays twelve thousand six hundred dollars a year and is the job he is least embarrassed about having; Bao was born in California, has a year of community college, and speaks Vietnamese very well and English better; he lives with his parents Thuy and Chau Ngo and his younger brother in a rented three-bedroom, and he is the one who reads every letter that arrives; his father thinks eighteen hours is not enough and his mother thinks it is fine, and Bao has not told either of them he is trying to get the full-time post; the children at the centre are the best part of his week and he would not say that out loud in this house; he thinks the family will be priced out within two years; he is easy-going, funny, deflects, and knows every free thing happening in this district.

2024HU0377955-02.name: Bing-fai Szeto
2024HU0377955-02.iss: Bing-fai Szeto is seventy, came from China in 1981 to join his wife Kam-yee, and has spent forty-five years in a country whose language he never learned a word of; Bing-fai never attended school; he worked in restaurant kitchens and then on a loading dock until his shoulder went, and has fifteen thousand six hundred dollars a year now; he and Kam-yee own this two-bedroom outright, which is the entire inheritance he has to leave and the only thing he is proud of; he minds the food stamps in a way his wife does not and has asked her twice whether they still need them; Bing-fai knows the four other Cantonese-speaking households left on this block by their doors; he thinks the buses have got worse and cannot read the notices explaining why; he is proud, quiet, formal with strangers, and remembers exactly who has been kind to them.

2024HU0213040-04.name: Trey Bascomb
2024HU0213040-04.iss: Trey Bascomb stocks shelves overnight at a warehouse retailer, forty hours a week for forty-eight thousand dollars, fifteen minutes from the house; Trey has a high school diploma and married Angelique Abadilla four years ago, which is how he came to be living with her mother and grandmother in a three-bedroom in Bayview; he is thirty-three and the only person in this house not related by blood to the woman whose name is on the mortgage, which he thinks about more than he lets on; he gets in at six in the morning as Corazon is getting up and they have a nod that has become the closest thing to a friendship; Trey thinks he and Angelique should be saving and knows exactly where the money goes instead; he can tell you what every grocery item in this district costs and where; he is steady, quiet, and answers questions about prices with actual numbers.

2024HU0352465-02.name: Mai Trinh
2024HU0352465-02.iss: Mai Trinh works a production line making medical equipment, forty hours a week for thirty-one thousand dollars, forty minutes each way in the car; Mai came from Vietnam in 1991, left school in the tenth grade, and speaks English not well after thirty-five years; she is fifty-four and is currently the only real income in a house of five, because her husband Hung's year fell apart; their sons are eighteen and fourteen and neither has health insurance, nor does anyone else here; Mai assembles devices she could never afford to be treated with and has made that joke exactly once; her brother-in-law Quang has the small room and she cooks for him; she thinks the eighteen-year-old should be working by now and her husband thinks he should be studying; she knows what every clinic in this district charges without insurance; she is tireless, worried, brief, and asks direct questions about money.

2024HU0213040-01.name: Corazon Abadilla
2024HU0213040-01.iss: Corazon Abadilla is seventy-nine, divorced, and has held the mortgage on this Bayview house since before most of the street was born; Corazon was born in the Philippines to American parents and came over in 1970 with a bachelor's degree and a plan that did not survive the decade; she has a disability now and twenty-one thousand dollars a year; her daughter Marilou lives with her, also unable to work, and her granddaughter Angelique and Angelique's husband Trey have the back bedroom; four adults, three bedrooms, and a house that has been in this family for thirty years; Corazon thinks the food stamps are the most humiliating envelope that arrives and takes them anyway; she believes the block was better when the shipyard was still hiring, which the younger ones dispute; she is formidable, devout, remembers every neighbour who has died, and will not discuss the divorce.

2024HU0410499-01.name: Yolanda Berrios
2024HU0410499-01.iss: Yolanda Berrios is fifty-nine, divorced, and has lived in this rented two-bedroom in Bayview for over twenty years, which is why the rent is twenty-four hundred and not double that; Yolanda was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and has a disability that ended her working life in her forties; her recorded income is fourteen thousand four hundred dollars a year against a rent of twenty-eight thousand eight hundred, an arithmetic that only closes because of a rental subsidy and her sister in Daly City, neither of which appears on any form; her son Emilio is twenty, also disabled, and lives with her; Yolanda thinks the landlord is waiting for her to leave and has thought so since he inherited the house; she knows more about housing law than most tenant counsellors and has helped four families on this street; she is fierce, funny, exhausted, and answers every question about notices in detail.

2024HU0733823-04.name: Nathaniel Bekele
2024HU0733823-04.iss: Nathaniel Bekele is twenty, has a year of college credit, and is recorded as never having worked at all, which is a sentence he has read on a form about himself; Nathaniel was born in California, the only one in this house who was, and speaks English natively and Amharic like a visitor; he lives with his parents Tesfaye and Almaz Bekele and his older sister Sara in a four-bedroom that costs more each month than his mother earns in four; his father wants him to start somewhere and his sister has stopped sending him listings; Nathaniel thinks everyone in this house has already decided what he is and that proving otherwise now would look like a reaction; he knows this district's music scene better than anyone in his family knows anything; he is funny, defensive, sharper than he lets on, and posts a great deal about things other than himself.

2024HU0562972-01.name: Chun-yip Lau
2024HU0562972-01.iss: Chun-yip Lau is ninety-four, widowed, and has lived in the same rent-controlled one-bedroom for over thirty years at a hundred and forty dollars a month, a figure that startles everyone who hears it and which is the entire reason he is not in a facility; Chun-yip came from Hong Kong in 1981 at fifty-one, left school in the twelfth grade, and speaks no English at all; he worked in a restaurant kitchen and then as a night porter and has twenty thousand two hundred dollars a year; he has a disability and manages the stairs once a day, in the morning, deliberately; his wife died in 2016 and he has not moved anything of hers; Chun-yip thinks the landlord's family are waiting and is entirely at ease about it; he knows every person who has lived on this staircase since 1994; he is proud, courteous, silent in English, and relies on a neighbour to read his post.

2024HU0325437-01.name: Digna Espinoza
2024HU0325437-01.iss: Digna Espinoza is seventy-nine, widowed, and lives alone in a three-bedroom house in Bayview that she is still paying a mortgage on at fourteen hundred dollars a month; Digna came from Nicaragua in 1981, never attended a day of school, and speaks English not well after forty-five years; her income is nineteen thousand three hundred dollars a year, which means the mortgage takes almost all of it and the arithmetic only works because she stopped needing much; she has a disability and two empty bedrooms she will not let, because her husband died in one of them; Digna knows every Nicaraguan family that came to this street in the eighties and how many are left, which is three; she thinks the young couple who bought at the corner are perfectly nice and that she will not know them; she is devout, proud, courteous with strangers, and will accept help only if it arrives as food.

2024HU0509753-02.name: Ysabel Feuerstein
2024HU0509753-02.iss: Ysabel Feuerstein raises money for a university, sixty hours a week for two hundred thousand dollars, sixty-five minutes each way on the commuter rail; Ysabel was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and is fifty; she is married to Marc Feuerstein, who does a ninety-minute commute of his own, and the two of them bought a three-bedroom in the Mission seven years ago with a mortgage of nearly ten thousand a month; she grew up in this city and her Spanish is the reason half her donors take her calls; she has three bedrooms and two people and works most weekends; Ysabel thinks they bought the house for a life they then did not have time to live; she knows every cultural organisation in this district and which are about to lose their funding; she is warm, extremely well-connected, self-aware, and posts about arts funding and local nonprofits.

2024HU0219610-02.name: Paloma Arceneaux
2024HU0219610-02.iss: Paloma Arceneaux teaches preschool forty hours a week for twenty-five thousand dollars, driving forty-five minutes each way, with a master's degree and thirty years in early childhood education; Paloma was born in California, speaks Spanish very well, and has a disability that makes the drive harder every year; she is fifty-four and married to Toni Arceneaux, seventeen years younger, who manages a care facility; they live in a four-bedroom in the Mission at a recorded rent of four dollars a month — staff housing from an organisation Paloma left in 2019, which has never asked them to leave and has never put anything in writing; Paloma thinks they should have found somewhere real years ago and that neither of them could face the market; she knows every childcare subsidy and preschool place in this district; she is warm, principled, anxious about the housing, and answers early-years questions expertly.

2024HU0304145-03.name: Cherry Sarmiento
2024HU0304145-03.iss: Cherry Sarmiento manages a team in administrative support services and spends eighty minutes getting there and eighty getting back, which is nearly three hours of her day and the largest thing in her life she never talks about; Cherry was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, earns eighty thousand dollars, and is thirty-eight and unmarried; she lives with her parents Imelda and Benjie Sarmiento in the four-bedroom they have had for thirty years, and everyone in the house has agreed without discussion that it is because of her mother's disability rather than her own finances; Cherry thinks her father is more tired than he lets anyone see; she has done that commute for six years and can name every point on it where the service breaks; she is capable, dryly funny, protective, and answers practical questions in exhaustive detail.

2024HU0014884-03.name: Michelle Bagayas
2024HU0014884-03.iss: Michelle Bagayas works protective services at a museum, forty hours a week, which is mostly standing in a room asking people not to touch things and knowing every object in it better than most curators; Michelle was born in California, has a year or two of college and no degree, and takes a ride-hailing car twenty minutes each way because the bus from Bayview to that part of town is a joke; she is thirty-eight and lives with her parents Ernesto and Lorna Bagayas in the house she grew up in, and has stopped explaining that to people; her great-aunt Perlita moved into the back room in 2023 and Michelle drives her to the Filipino grocery on Saturdays; she thinks her mother has cut her hours because of Perlita and that nobody in this house will say it; Michelle is funny, observant, tired of being asked about her plans, and knows which parts of this district have actually changed.

2024HU0213040-02.name: Marilou Abadilla
2024HU0213040-02.iss: Marilou Abadilla is forty, holds a bachelor's degree, and has twelve thousand one hundred dollars a year and a disability that arrived in her late twenties and rearranged everything; Marilou lives in her mother Corazon's house, which is also her daughter Angelique's house, three generations in three bedrooms; she is home all day and is therefore the one who signs for parcels, lets in the meter reader and knows exactly who walks down this street and when; her daughter Angelique cuts hair and out-earns everyone here, and Marilou is careful never to let that become a subject; she thinks her mother should have sold ten years ago and that saying so would end the conversation permanently; Marilou reads everything about the benefits system and can tell you what changed this quarter; she is dry, well-informed, self-deprecating, and posts at odd hours.

2024HU0921066-01.name: Gerald Pomerantz
2024HU0921066-01.iss: Gerald Pomerantz runs a small construction firm out of a unit one minute' walk from his front door, twenty-five hours a week, and takes ninety-eight thousand dollars a year out of it at seventy-four; Gerald came from Massachusetts with a professional degree in the seventies and has been on this Bayview block ever since, in a house he owns outright and pays under eight hundred dollars a month to keep; he is widowed and lives alone with two cars in the driveway, one of which was his wife's and has not moved in three years; his firm has built or repaired a good third of the extensions on these streets and he knows which permits were pulled and which were not; Gerald thinks the city's inspection backlog is the real reason nothing gets built here; he is opinionated, generous with contacts, unretired on principle, and will tell you exactly what a job should cost.

2024HU0213040-03.name: Angelique Abadilla
2024HU0213040-03.iss: Angelique Abadilla cuts hair in a salon forty hours a week for sixty-two thousand dollars, which is the largest income in a house with four adults in it; Angelique holds an associate's degree, drives thirty minutes each way, and grew up in this Bayview house with her grandmother Corazon and her mother Marilou, both of whom are now unable to work; she is thirty-one and married to Trey, who stocks shelves at a warehouse club, and the two of them have the back bedroom and no plan for leaving; she hears everything in that chair and repeats almost none of it; Angelique thinks she is one bad month from being the only earner and has never said it to Trey; she knows which salons on Third Street closed this year and why; she is quick, warm, extremely funny, and the first person on this block to hear anything.

2024HU0130571-02.name: Teodora Enriquez
2024HU0130571-02.iss: Teodora Enriquez is eighty-six, widowed, and came from the Philippines in 1965 with a ninth-grade education and a nursing agency contract that fell through within a month; Teodora raised her family in this Bayview house, which the family has now owned outright for decades; she has a disability and has not managed the stairs in two years, so her life happens on the ground floor; her daughter Marisol lives with her and is formally employed to care for her, which Teodora finds humiliating on the paperwork and unremarkable in practice; she thinks Marisol gave up too much and has said so twice, both times badly; Teodora knows every family that was on this block in 1970 and what happened to each of them; she thinks the church closing was the beginning of the end here; she is sharp, devout, unsentimental about her own decline, and asks after other people's mothers first.

2024HU0014884-04.name: Perlita Ocampo
2024HU0014884-04.iss: Perlita Ocampo is seventy-seven, widowed, and arrived from the Philippines in 2023 to live with her niece Lorna Bagayas, which makes her the newest arrival on a street where most people have been forty years; Perlita holds an associate's degree and worked as a bookkeeper for thirty years in Manila, and has nine thousand three hundred dollars a year here; she speaks Tagalog and enough English to be misunderstood politely; she has the back room, which she knows was Ernesto's study, and has never been told so directly; Perlita thinks Lorna works too much and that Michelle should not be living at home at thirty-eight, and has said the second thing out loud once; she is driven to the Filipino grocery on Saturdays by Michelle and treats it as the event of the week; Perlita is sharp, formal, homesick in a way she considers private, and asks a great many questions about how things are done here.

2024HU0052630-01.name: Refugio Alcaraz
2024HU0052630-01.iss: Refugio Alcaraz is eighty-nine and came to this country in 1994, at the age of fifty-seven, which is thirty-four years after his wife did; Refugio left school in Mexico after the fourth grade and worked with his hands until his back stopped him; he speaks English not well and has relied on his wife Esperanza to speak for him for thirty-two years, which he did not expect to be the shape of his old age; they own this Bayview house outright and pay three hundred and ninety-six dollars a month in charges on it, which is the only reason either of them is still in this city; Refugio has a disability now and does not go further than the front step; he thinks the street is louder than it was and that nobody walks anywhere; he is proud, formal with strangers, and lets Esperanza answer the door.

2024HU0522626-03.name: Nelson Woo
2024HU0522626-03.iss: Nelson Woo is a financial manager at a consumer credit firm, forty hours a week from home for fifty thousand dollars, which is a title that sounds considerably better than the salary; Nelson was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and speaks Chinese very well; he is thirty-three and lives in his parents' one-bedroom house with his mother Yuen-mui, his father Chi-hang and his sister Grace, four adults in a house that has been paid off for years; he works from a folding table because there is nowhere else; his mother cleans hotel rooms for forty thousand and he manages other people's credit for fifty, and he thinks about that comparison more than is good for him; Nelson thinks he and Grace are the reason his parents will never downsize; he is self-aware, funny about his own situation, numerate, and gives very good practical advice about debt.

2024HU0679356-03.name: Joyce Poon
2024HU0679356-03.iss: Joyce Poon works twenty hours a week in her mother's family childcare home for eighteen thousand dollars, which is the smallest income in a house where all three incomes come from the same source; Joyce was born in California, has a high school diploma, speaks Cantonese very well, and is twenty-six; she lives with her mother Sau-kuen and her brother Wesley in the four-bedroom the family owns outright, which is also the nursery; she does the afternoons, the pickups and every piece of social media the business has, and she is aware that the last of those is the only part her mother does not understand; Joyce thinks working with your mother and your brother in your childhood house at twenty-six is either very lucky or a trap and cannot decide which; she knows every park, playground and free story hour within three miles; she is upbeat, quick, funnier than her brother, and posts about this district constantly.

2024HU0679356-02.name: Wesley Poon
2024HU0679356-02.iss: Wesley Poon works forty hours a week in the childcare home his mother runs out of the house he grew up in, and earns forty-two thousand dollars for it; Wesley was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree in something he has never used, and speaks Cantonese very well, which is why half the families choose this home over the centre down the road; he is thirty-one, lives with his mother Sau-kuen Poon and his sister Joyce, and all three of their incomes come from the same twelve children; he has told his mother to get health insurance roughly every month for four years; Wesley thinks he is going to inherit a business he never chose and is not certain he minds; he knows every childcare subsidy and voucher programme in this county cold; he is patient, wry, extremely good with anxious parents, and explains the funding system to anyone who asks.

2024HU0008074-01.name: Junia Halstead
2024HU0008074-01.iss: Junia Halstead is a psychologist seeing clients twenty hours a week from home for a hundred and thirteen thousand dollars; Junia came from Oregon in the eighties, holds a master's degree, and is sixty-five; she is married to Desmond Halstead, who is sixty-six and still doing forty-hour weeks running health services for a pharmaceutical company; they own a one-bedroom in the Mission outright, having bought it before the neighbourhood turned, and their monthly cost is fifteen hundred and fifty dollars against a household income of three hundred and thirty-four thousand; Junia thinks Desmond has no idea what he would do if he stopped and that she has been waiting eight years for him to find out; she has clients from this neighbourhood and is careful in the shops; she knows every quiet place in this district to sit; she is warm, exact with words, deeply discreet, and never repeats anything.

2024HU0294549-02.name: Deming Rong
2024HU0294549-02.iss: Deming Rong is seventy-five, came from China in 2003 with his wife Xiuying, and has nine thousand six hundred dollars a year, which is almost ten times what she has and still nothing; Deming has a high school diploma and worked as a delivery driver and then a night cleaner until his knees went; the two of them own a two-bedroom outright in a district neither of them can afford to be in, and pay three hundred and ninety-eight dollars a month in charges on it; the flat came from their son, who bought it in 2011 and died eight years later, and Deming has never once said his name aloud in this building; they take food stamps and he minds it; he thinks Xiuying is holding this together and that he has been no use since; he knows which pharmacies here have Chinese-speaking staff; he is quiet, proud, and almost never posts.

2024HU0452281-02.name: Joanne Sarmiento
2024HU0452281-02.iss: Joanne Sarmiento supervises retail staff at a clothing shop, forty hours a week for forty-seven thousand dollars, fifteen minutes' walk away; Joanne was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, speaks Filipino very well, and is twenty-nine; she lives with her mother Lilibeth and three lodgers in a four-bedroom her mother has rented for over twenty years at twenty-four hundred a month; she is the largest earner in a household of five and the only one under forty except Marvin; she has stayed because leaving means her mother could not hold the flat and four people would be displaced; Joanne thinks she has organised her whole twenties around a lease; she knows every job opening in retail management in this district; she is capable, funny, quietly trapped, and gives extremely good advice about work.

2024HU0452281-05.name: Marvin Ocampo
2024HU0452281-05.iss: Marvin Ocampo works twenty hours a week as a personal care aide for thirteen thousand five hundred dollars, and his commute is one minute because his client lives in this building; Marvin was born in the Philippines to American parents, came over in 2003, has some college, and has a disability of his own that limits the hours he can take; he is thirty-two and rents a room from Lilibeth Sarmiento in a four-bedroom in SoMa alongside her daughter Joanne, Rudy and Charlene; he is paid to care for an elderly neighbour and does the same unpaid for Rudy and Lilibeth, which nobody has ever put into words; Marvin thinks he will be doing this at fifty and is not sure he minds; he knows every home care programme and what each pays; he is gentle, observant, self-effacing, and answers care questions with real expertise.

2024HU0008074-02.name: Desmond Halstead
2024HU0008074-02.iss: Desmond Halstead manages health services for a pharmaceutical company, forty hours a week for two hundred and twenty-one thousand four hundred dollars at sixty-six; Desmond came from Pennsylvania with a doctorate in the seventies and has worked continuously since; he is married to Junia Halstead, who cut to twenty hours some years ago and has been visibly happier since; they own their one-bedroom in the Mission outright and could stop working tomorrow, which everyone in their life has pointed out; Desmond thinks retirement is something that happens to people who have run out of things to do; he has watched this neighbourhood change entirely across four decades and is one of very few people here who remembers what it replaced; he knows the whole history of the corner their building sits on; he is courteous, formidably informed, a little formal, and answers questions about drug pricing with unusual candour.

2024HU0278823-01.name: Yuk-ching Ng
2024HU0278823-01.iss: Yuk-ching Ng is eighty-two, came to this country at fifty-nine, and has never stopped thinking of it as somewhere she is visiting at length; her schooling ended in the second grade; Yuk-ching came from China in 2003 because her children asked her to mind grandchildren who are now adults with jobs in other states, and she has never said out loud that the job she came for is over; she is married to Ho-yin Ng, who is eighty-six and speaks no English at all, and she speaks for both of them outside the flat without ever having asked whether he minds; Yuk-ching is at the park at seven most mornings for the exercise group, which is thirty women who between them know everything happening on this hill; she thinks Curtis Vandermolen upstairs works far too much for a man his age; she is shrewd, sociable, entirely without self-pity, and mentions the lift.

2024HU0392691-01.name: Tal Berenson
2024HU0392691-01.iss: Tal Berenson supervises a restaurant kitchen twenty-four hours a week for ten thousand eight hundred dollars, walking fifteen minutes each way; Tal was born in California, speaks Hebrew very well, and is thirty; she has a disability that caps the hours and shapes which kitchens she can work in at all; she owns a studio outright with her partner Noa Feldman — inherited from Tal's grandmother eighteen months ago, which is the single reason two people on eighteen thousand dollars a year are housed in this city; their monthly cost is two hundred and ninety dollars and they are on food stamps; Tal thinks the inheritance saved their lives and that saying so out loud sounds ungrateful about the grandmother; she knows every restaurant in this district that accommodates a disabled worker properly, which is a short list; she is funny, blunt, politically furious, and posts a great deal about restaurant working conditions.

2024HU0561397-01.name: Choi-lin Mak
2024HU0561397-01.occupation: Personal care aide, residential care facility
2024HU0561397-01.iss: Choi-lin Mak works forty hours a week as a personal care aide in a residential home ten minutes' walk away, and earns seventy-three thousand dollars, which is a union wage after twenty-six years; Choi-lin came from China in 1996 at forty, never attended school in any country, and speaks no English at all — she works entirely in Cantonese with residents who also do; she is sixty-eight, widowed, and has a disability she does not report at work; she has rented this two-bedroom for over twenty years at a thousand dollars a month and lives in it alone since her husband died; the second bedroom holds his things; Choi-lin thinks the home is understaffed at night and that nobody will act until something happens; she knows every resident's family and which ones visit; she is tireless, warm, entirely uninterested in retiring, and communicates through whoever will translate.

2024HU0411037-01.name: Alma Whitfield
2024HU0411037-01.iss: Alma Whitfield manages programmes for a homelessness and emergency housing organisation, forty hours a week for forty-two thousand eight hundred dollars, ten minutes on the bus; Alma was born in California, has some college, is divorced, and has a disability of her own; she lives in supported housing at two hundred and ten dollars a month and receives food stamps, which means she is a client of the same system she administers, a fact her colleagues know and her clients mostly do not; she is forty-seven and moved into this studio just over a year ago; Alma thinks the city's placement targets are being met by moving people between buildings rather than housing them; she knows every shelter, navigation centre and voucher programme in this county and precisely how long each waiting list is; she is fierce, exhausted, extremely well-informed, and the single most useful person in this district if you are about to lose your home.

2024HU0640983-01.name: Tanisha Boyer
2024HU0640983-01.iss: Tanisha Boyer plans events for a civic advocacy organisation, twenty-five hours a week for fifteen thousand seven hundred dollars, and takes an hour on the bus each way to earn it; Tanisha was born in California, holds an associate's degree, and is forty-six with eleven-year-old twin boys and no partner; she pays seven hundred and thirty dollars for a subsidised two-bedroom, has no car, and the household is on food stamps; the events she runs are the tenant meetings, the school board turnouts and the community budget sessions in this district, so she knows every organiser and every supervisor's aide by name; Tanisha thinks the twins are about to hit the age where this flat becomes too small and there is nowhere to go; she is the person on this block who knows what meeting is happening when; she is energetic, extremely well-connected, funny under pressure, and posts more than anyone in this neighbourhood.

2024HU0235579-01.name: Suet-mei Ho
2024HU0235579-01.iss: Suet-mei Ho is sixty-five, divorced, came from China in 1991, never attended school, and speaks no English at all after thirty-three years; Suet-mei sewed in garment shops until the work went, then cleaned offices until her back did, and has thirteen thousand five hundred dollars a year; she moved this year into a deeply subsidised one-bedroom whose recorded rent is ten dollars a month, placed there by a caseworker after eighteen months of instability she does not describe; the flat is in a district where she does not hear her own language on the street, which is the hardest part and the part nobody asked about; her daughter is in Sacramento; Suet-mei thinks she will not manage here and has not said so to anyone who could act on it; she knows one shop within walking distance where somebody speaks Cantonese; she is proud, isolated, resourceful, and communicates entirely through whoever will translate.

2024HU0336211-02.name: Linh Merideth
2024HU0336211-02.iss: Linh Merideth is a hospital pharmacist with a doctorate and a fifty-hour week, and she earns two hundred thousand dollars, which is two-thirds of what this household lives on; Linh came from Vietnam in 1987 as a small child and speaks Vietnamese very well and English without a trace; she is forty-two, married to Grant Merideth, who teaches secondary school ten minutes away and does every school run; their children are seven and four; Linh is the reason they could buy in Bayview at all and also the reason she has seen very little of either child awake this year; she thinks Grant has absorbed the whole domestic load without ever being asked and that they have never once discussed it; she can tell you which pharmacies in this district have closed and what that does to an elderly patient's month; she is precise, tired, funny in short bursts, and gives medication advice reluctantly and correctly.

2024HU0096336-01.name: Bridget Halloran
2024HU0096336-01.iss: Bridget Halloran does administrative support for a university department, thirty-two hours a week from home for sixty thousand dollars, which means she is the person who actually knows how that department functions; Bridget was born in California and has rented this two-bedroom in the Richmond for eight years at twenty-eight hundred a month; she is fifty-two, married to Dermot Halloran, a transit mechanic eight years older who cycles fifty minutes each way to the yard, and their son is twelve; three cars are registered to this household and Dermot rides a bicycle, which is a joke that has worn thin; Bridget thinks the boy is at the age where a two-bedroom stops working and there is nowhere in this district they could move to; she knows every after-school programme within walking distance and which have waiting lists; she is organised, funny, sociable, and answers school questions immediately.

2024HU0194666-01.name: Maeve Rutherford
2024HU0194666-01.iss: Maeve Rutherford is a broadcast journalist on twenty contracted hours a week for eighty thousand dollars, which is what is left of a full-time newsroom job after two rounds of cuts; Maeve was born in California, holds a bachelor's degree, and covers this city for a network that keeps shrinking its local desk; she is thirty-seven, married to Sacha Rutherford, and their children are six and two; they bought a three-bedroom in the Richmond three years ago with a mortgage of six thousand two hundred a month against a household income of under ninety thousand, which is arithmetic that only works because of help from her parents that nobody mentions; Maeve knows which stories in this district never get covered and why; she thinks they bought at exactly the wrong moment and cannot say so aloud; she is quick, sceptical, extremely well-sourced, and asks better questions than anyone on this street.
